e1rm.label: What is estimated 1RM?
e1rm.body:
1RM (one-rep max) is the heaviest weight you could lift once.

You don't have to test it: it's estimated from your regular sets with the Epley formula: weight × (1 + reps ÷ 30). E.g. 80 kg × 8 ≈ 101 kg.

This lets you compare sets with different rep counts: if it goes up, you're getting stronger.
e1rm.yours: This value comes from the set {weight} kg × {reps}: {weight} × (1 + {reps} ÷ 30) = {value} kg.

maxWeight.label: Max weight
maxWeight.body:
The heaviest weight used in any completed set, regardless of reps.

Not the same as 1RM: 70 kg × 8 means a max weight of 70 kg, but an estimated 1RM of ≈ 89 kg.

bestSet.label: Set volume
bestSet.body:
Your best weight × reps in a single set. E.g. 80 kg × 10 = 800 kg.

It rewards sets where you did a lot of work at once, even if the weight wasn't a record.

volume.label: Volume (tonnage)
volume.body:
The sum of weight × reps across all completed sets. E.g. 3 sets of 80 kg × 10 = 2400 kg.

It measures the total work you did. Bodyweight sets (e.g. plank) count as 0.

avgSets.label: Sets per workout
avgSets.body: Average number of completed sets per workout in the selected range. Unchecked sets don't count.

topGroup.label: Most trained muscle group
topGroup.body: The muscle group with the most completed sets in the range. Each exercise counts toward its main muscle group.

adherence.label: Plan adherence
adherence.body:
Compares workouts scheduled in the Planner with what you actually did.

Skipped: you marked it as skipped. Missed: its day passed and it was never started.

Workouts planned for today or later don't count toward the percentage.

weekly.label: How to read this chart
weekly.body:
Each bar is one week (Monday–Sunday); its height is the volume: weight × reps summed over all completed sets that week.

The dashed line is the average of complete weeks. The lighter bar is the current week, still in progress.

Hover (or tap) a bar to see that week's details.

weeklyChange.label: Weekly change
weeklyChange.body:
Volume of the last complete week compared with the average of the {weeks} weeks before it.

The current week is ignored because it isn't over. A drop of tens of percent usually means fewer workouts that week or a planned deload.

streak.label: Streak
streak.body:
Weekly streak: how many consecutive weeks had at least one workout. The current week without a workout doesn't break it yet.

Days in a row: consecutive days with a workout, counting from today or yesterday. With every-other-day training it's usually 0–1, which is fine.

muscles.label: Sets per week
muscles.body:
Average completed sets per week for each muscle group in the selected range.

The green band (10–20 sets) is a commonly recommended range for building muscle. Below it is “too few”; above it is “a lot”: it can work, but recovery gets harder.

Each exercise counts only toward its main muscle group, so e.g. triceps work from bench press isn't included. Cardio and full-body exercises aren't rated.

repRanges.label: Rep ranges
repRanges.body:
1–5: heavy and short, mostly builds strength.

6–12: the classic muscle-building range.

13+: lighter and longer, builds muscular endurance.

There's no single right split; it should match your goal.

stagnation.label: When is an exercise stalled?
stagnation.body:
An exercise shows up here when:

• you do it regularly (within the last 3 weeks),

• your best estimated 1RM is more than 6 weeks old,

• you've had at least 3 sessions since.

Matching a record doesn't count as a new one. Changing the rep range, the exercise variation or getting more rest can help.

records.label: Records
records.body:
Est. 1RM: best estimated weight for 1 rep. Max weight: heaviest weight used. Set volume: best weight × reps in one set.

The gold trophy means one of these records was set in the selected range.

repRecords.label: What does 5RM mean?
repRecords.body:
5RM is the heaviest weight you've lifted for at least 5 reps. Same for 1RM, 3RM, 8RM and so on.

A 70 kg × 8 set qualifies for 1, 3, 5 and 8 reps, so if you've never lifted anything heavier, the same set is the record in several tiles.

1RM here is weight actually lifted, not estimated. You'll find the estimate in the records above.

repRecordActual.label: Record from a {actual}-rep set
repRecordActual.body:
There's no heavier set for {reps}–{below} reps yet, so the {reps}RM record is the {weight} kg × {actual} set.

If you managed {actual} reps, you could lift it {reps} times, and probably more weight.
